skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: The warning at T2 came before any substantive question and said the firm represents the Committee and the company only, not the witness, and cannot give him legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explained that the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose what is learned without the witness's consent or notice.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 set out how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, required speculation to be flagged, and asked the witness to separate recollection from reconstruction.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asked the witness to restate in his own words who the firm represents and who controls privilege, and T5 showed he understood; questions were invited at T2.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T68 covered confidentiality, document and notes retention, not speaking with other witnesses, possible follow-up, and asked whether there was anything to add or correct.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
The company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what we learn, including to the government, without your consent and without telling you.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
A few ground rules: if you're speculating, assuming, or estimating, please tell me.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: T14 invited an open narrative of how LJM1 came about, but later topics such as Chewco and Southampton were mostly put as narrow questions rather than open invitations.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The sequence ran from role (T8) to the open LJM1 narrative (T14) to compensation, Southampton, Chewco and controls, which is a sensible general-to-specific order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were clear, such as T20 and T58, but T42 combined three recipients and T56 presupposed that Causey and Buy reviewed every deal.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stayed neutral and polite, but the interviewer accepted the witness's repeated non-answers at T51 and T29 without regaining control of the topic.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer adjusted to the answers, pressing on the Foundation's $4.5 million at T38 and T40 and on the approval sheets at T60, but did not follow the new leads the witness opened.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Let's start with your role. As CFO, what were you responsible for?
How do you know Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy reviewed every LJM2 deal?
Our information is roughly $4.5 million, about six weeks after it invested. Does that fit your memory?
Put the Foundation's $4.5 million receipt against the witness's earlier statement to the Board about not receiving Enron stock value.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer did not press the non-answers: T20 and T21 ended with 'That was me, as I said', T29 was accepted, and T55's 'I don't recall' was not tested against the witness's presence on the call.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked who negotiated (T26), who invested (T32), what the Foundation put in and received (T34), and when (T38), covering who, what and when.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The main attempts were giving the $4.5 million figure at T38 and showing the minutes at T52; no other method was tried when the witness said he did not recall.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: T58 asked whether the witness checked the approvals, and he answered 'No. I didn't check each one myself.', which separated his knowledge from assumption.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T66 asked who else should be spoken to and the witness named five people, but the interviewer did not follow up on any of them.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The witness mentioned the resolution, the minutes and the Foundation's statements, but the interviewer requested none of these; only the approval sheets were raised, and only through questions.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: T24 asked how sure the witness was about what he told the Board, and T56 to T59 tested how well he knew the LJM2 review.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up well on the undisclosed Foundation investment at T41 to T45, but let 'The sheets would show the rest' at T63 pass without follow-up.

moments.text: Who raised it with them first?
That was me, as I said.
How sure are you that's what you told them?
Very sure. It's in the resolution and the minutes.
So that I have it right: none of them was told?
Did you check that it was followed?
No. I didn't check each one myself.
Who else should we speak with?
The Foundation's statements would have the exact figure.
Which ones?
Raptor I is the one I remember. The sheets would show the rest.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The minutes were shown at T52 with recognition and an authentication question, but there was no prior memory question and no context on when or why the witness saw them.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The document was put to the witness before any account of the November 1997 call was taken, and T54 went straight to the question of whether Kopper's role was mentioned.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: T52 identified the document by its title and date, and the interviewer did not misdescribe its contents.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: T54 asked a neutral question and drew no conclusion from the minutes.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: After T55's denial, the interviewer moved straight to LJM2 controls without asking the witness to reconcile his answer with what the minutes showed or with his earlier account.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
Do they mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?
No, they don't. I don't recall it being discussed on the call.
I don't, really. That was the requirement, and I assumed it was followed.

tips: Before I show you the November 5, 1997 minutes, what do you remember about who was on that call and what was said about who would manage Chewco?
Which approval sheets do you believe were signed after closing, besides Raptor I, and where would we find them?
